Q: Flutter : How to change Android minSdkVersion in Flutter Project? A:

** 2026 UPDATED **

***

Flutter version 3.32 (and may be greater)***

If you can't find minSdk, compileSdk or targerSDK and all you see is

targetSdkVersion flutter.targetSdkVersion
minSdkVersion flutter.minSdkVersion
compileSdkVersion flutter.compileSdkVersion

Then you can go to where your flutter main folder is and from there

the address is ***flutter-directory/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/***FlutterExtension.kt

Inside FlutterExtension.kt you can see the code

class FlutterExtension {

  /** Sets the compileSdkVersion used by default in Flutter app projects. */
  public final int compileSdkVersion = 36

  /** Sets the minSdkVersion used by default in Flutter app projects. */
  public  final int minSdkVersion = 26

  /**
  * Sets the targetSdkVersion used by default in Flutter app projects.
  * targetSdkVersion should always be the latest available stable version.
  *
  * See https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.
  */
  public final int targetSdkVersion = 36
}

Change your TargetSdkVersion, minSdkVersion, compileSdkVersion from here.

Q: Why is try/catch within nested for loops substantially slowing down execution time? A:

Since I do not know C#'s internals regarding exceptions very well, this will be a general explanation of exception handling based on my experience with different CPUs/systems (which should in theory apply here too):

Generally, there should be no runtime-overhead associated with setting up a try/catch-block. It is possible, and common (ie x64) to move all the required unwind-data into meta-data, and the "catch" code into some external frame/end of the current frame, so that it is never actually touched/executed unless an exception is thrown. There may be some cost technically due to the presence of this meta-data, but this should not matter outside of an slighty increase in executable size and related load-time increases.

The cost actually does come from throwing the exception - this will be a very costly process. In an aformentioned implementation, the runtime will need to access this meta-data, and evaluate it. It needs to simulate a stack-unwind to find the correct handler (even if it is located right next to the source of the exception), and then invoke the handler and do some other work (unsure how much frame-teardown logic actually needs to be run for C#, outside of usings). Regardless, this will be very costly.

What does that mean in practice? Exceptions are reserved for exceptional situations/unexpected errors. None of that applies to your case, at least not as-written.
Either your out-of-bounds access is an actual mistake in the loop/calculations, in which case the solution is not to "try/catch", but to fix that error.
Or it is well-defined that the code might actually touch beyond the current array-data, with a well-defined value "0" (which would make sense for a texture-filter type calculation) - in which case, you use explicit checks. This is not only faster for this situation, but also more clear - as again, the convention is generally to expect a "try/catch" for erroneous behaviour.
The last case (that I don't think applies for your situation): If you have code that accepts some user-input and uses it to process some nested-loop-value, and the out-of-bounds access is due to a user-input-error: Then you may consider validating that the input-values are in range before executing the loop, and potentially throw an exception to the user (to allow them to be notified of/handle that scenario).

Q: Visual Studio Code "The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'crashed', code: '-2147483645')" A:

If you landed here because you're using cursor, this is for you. I got the same error, but it was error code 7.

"The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'crashed', code: '7')"

My machine crashed while I was connected to a session and I wasn't able to clean it up. Whether it's a remote connection or local, on your local machine I had to run the following to clear out the existing settings and reset it:

rm -f ~/.config/Cursor/storage.json
rm -rf ~/.config/Cursor/Backups
rm -f ~/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb ~/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb-journal

Heads up - this basically resets cursor, but it resolves the issue.
